status: new, left over from the fix
title: On the D notes the register fix is weaker, because the D4 accent string is outside listen.reg
detail: listen.reg works for every note: the loudest string is the written note an octave up for all 78 theme notes, and the contour matches Grieg's at every step. But harpNote still adds the fixed D4 accent string on each D at 0.5x amplitude. On a main D, that accent and the D4 octave copy together carry almost as much energy as the D5 copy that should lead. The margin is 0.9 to 3.5 dB (mean 1.9 dB). On other notes the next copy is 4.4 dB down by design, and at least 2.7 dB down as recorded. So the Ds' octave is the least clear. In bars 1 and 3, B4 to D5 could be heard as B4 down to D4, a sixth down instead of a third up. This needs ears: check it in the planned phone listening test.
evidence: Recorded Listen along as the app plays it (worklet, desktop 1440x900, test/sound_rec.js tap, 16 kHz in this headless run), with each cue's frequency and amplitude logged. Dominant copy minus the written pitch: +12 semitones for 78 of 78 theme notes. Contour mismatches between consecutive main notes, by dominant copy: 0. On main D notes, D4 (copy plus accent) against D5, as root-sum-square amplitude: min -3.5, max -0.9, mean -1.9 dB, n = 18.
fix: When o.reg is given (a piece), put the D accent at the dominant copy's octave or leave it out. That is one condition in harpNote and does not change the pointer harp. Then re-run t_seasong.js.

title: 60 fps while it plays could not be confirmed here: seasong_cmd.js fails its four fps checks, and the cause is the machine
detail: seasong_cmd.js passes every check except the frame-time ones: desktop 17 fps (p95 115 ms), phone 8.5 to 15 fps. In the same session the app idle measured 15 fps (p95 115 ms), as low as during playback. An ordinary Listen along measured 16.5 fps and the piece 15.8 fps. So the low numbers come from the machine, not the feature. During the run another agent's headless Chrome (work/xv152/test/fx152_cdp, about 1 h old, its GPU helper at 114% CPU) and GeForce NOW were running, and the load average was 7.8. The piece now keeps up to 24 strings, not 12, which is more work on the audio worklet. AS-BUILT's 60 fps (p95 17.2 to 18.6 ms) may still hold, but it was not re-measured here.
evidence: test/verify_cdp/fps_cmd.js on port 9308: idle 14.9 / 14.8 / 14.7 fps; piece 15.8 fps; ordinary listen 16.5 fps. seasong_cmd.js: framesDesk {fps 17.1, p95 114.7}, phones {15.2, 8.9, 8.5 fps}. ps showed pid 28128 (fx152_cdp) and GeForceNOW.
fix: Re-run seasong_cmd.js (and v15_phone_cmd.js) when no other headless Chrome is running, before the merge. No code change is indicated.
